page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.4xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual server built on Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. Configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz. The instance includes a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside dedicated network bandwidth with a baseline speed of 25 Gbps. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark results place the m6idn.4xlarge consistently in the middle 50% across CPU, memory, and application-level workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1648.0, a multi-core score of 9891.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 21074.8. Under stress-ng, it produces 1890.79 single-core and 15409.45 multi-core metrics. Memory subsystem tests report read-only throughput of 97.47 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 57.21 GB/sec for large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by a PassMark database score of 7782.69 and 16.8 million Redis SET operations per second.

The presence of high-speed local NVMe storage and 25 Gbps network bandwidth increases resource density and operational efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads, eliminating latency bottlenecks associated with purely network-attached volumes. However, as an instance store, the 950 GB NVMe volume is ephemeral, meaning data does not persist across instance stop and start cycles.

This server type is suitable for balanced production environments that require fast local scratch storage and high baseline network throughput, such as relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, batch processing, CI/CD runners, and medium-scale web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, a 25 Gbps network baseline, and 950 GB of attached NVMe SSD instance storage, without hardware GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates consistent mid-range performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 9891.0, 16.8 million Redis SET operations per second, and 22.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. The inclusion of bundled local NVMe storage enhances I/O-bound workflows, though the storage is ephemeral and requires consideration for persistence. The instance is well matched for mid-sized database workloads, distributed caching, web application hosting, and data processing tasks requiring balanced compute and high network bandwidth.
